title: Nuevo Laredo Launches Gun Buyback: Cash for Firearms at Monumento a Los Fundadores
excerpt: The Mexican Army and the Nuevo Laredo municipal government have launched a voluntary gun buyback campaign, offering cash for firearms turned in at the Monumento
content:
The Mexican Army and the Nuevo Laredo municipal government have launched a voluntary gun buyback campaign, offering cash for firearms turned in at the Monumento a Los Fundadores.

The campaign, “¡Sí al desarme, sí a la paz!” — “Yes to disarmament, yes to peace!” — runs from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Nov. 18, 19, 23 and 24, 2026. Residents can turn in firearms of any type — long guns, handguns and hunting weapons of any caliber — and receive a cash payment set by an official military valuation schedule.

The effort is led by Gen. Humberto Ortega Ramírez, commander of the local military garrison, and Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal.

Speaking to reporters Nov. 18, Lt. Col. Isaac López Cabrera, second commander of the 29th Regiment, described the city as “very calm” and said the Army’s last armed confrontation in the city dated to February 2015.

How many firearms were turned in on the first day, and the exact cash amounts paid per weapon type, had not been published as of this writing. The campaign continues today, Nov. 19, at the Monumento a Los Fundadores from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.

The buyback is part of a national disarmament push in Mexico, where the federal government has promoted voluntary firearm exchanges as a way to reduce gun violence and keep weapons out of criminal hands.

Sources: CML Noticias, Nov. 17, 2026; Valle del Norte, Nov. 17, 2026; Manifiesto Tamaulipas, Nov. 18, 2026.
